name: অলন্দুরৈনাথর মন্দির, তিরুপ্পুল্লমঙ্গৈ
deity: অলন্দুরৈনাথর (ব্রহ্মপুরীশ্বরর) রূপে শিব, দেবী অল্লিয়ঙ্কোতৈ-র সঙ্গে
period: তেবারম যুগ (৭ম শতাব্দীতে গীত); আদি চোল মন্দির, আনু. ১০ম শতাব্দী
summary: পুল্লমঙ্গৈ, তাঞ্জাবুরের কাছে কুড়মুরুট্টির ধারে, শিবকে অলন্দুরৈনাথর রূপে — ব্রহ্মপুরীশ্বরর — দেবী অল্লিয়ঙ্কোতৈর সঙ্গে সম্মান করে। তিরুজ্ঞান সম্বন্দর কর্তৃক গীত একটি পাডল পেট্র স্থলম্, এর আদি-চোল মন্দিরটি তার যুগের কিছু সূক্ষ্মতম ও মনোরম প্রস্তর ভাস্কর্যের জন্য পণ্ডিতদের মধ্যে বিখ্যাত।

sections.history: Pullamangai, at Pasupathikoil on the banks of the Kudamurutti near Thanjavur, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. Its shrine is one of the celebrated early-Chola temples, of about the 10th century; historians rank its sculpture among the most remarkable of the early Chola age. The place was once a banyan forest by the riverbank, whence the name Alanthurai — 'the banyan ghat.'
sections.architecture: A compact early-Chola temple of exquisite workmanship, the shrine enshrines Alanthurainathar — Brahmapureeswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Alliyankothai in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. Its vimana is covered with finely carved niches and miniature figures — dvarapalas, Ganesha, Durga, the dikpalas and narrative panels — whose delicacy has made the temple a touchstone for the study of early Chola art.
sections.legends: The lord is worshipped as Alanthurainathar, 'lord of the banyan ghat,' and as Brahmapureeswarar, the lord of Brahma's city, worshipped also as Pasupatinathar. The goddess is Alliyankothai. As with the early-Chola shrines of the delta, the sthala tradition is bound up with the river Kudamurutti and the banyan forest that gave the place its name; Sambandar's verses carry its praise.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Scholars and pilgrims of the early-Chola trail come to Pullamangai both for darshan and for its celebrated sculpture.
sections.experience: At Pullamangai the pilgrim stands before one of the jewels of early-Chola building. Before Alanthurainathar and Alliyankothai, among the finely carved niches of the vimana, by the Kudamurutti's bank, the visitor finds both the grace of a Tevaram shrine and the quiet astonishment of its tenth-century stone.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Pullamangai (Pasupathikoil) lies on the Kudamurutti near Thanjavur, in Thanjavur district, a short way off the Thanjavur–Kumbakonam road. Thanjavur is the nearest city and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
